gap: No result ChatGPT got states the measured inverter-on idle draw of the stations in these kits: about 10 W for the Anker SOLIX S5000 (Andrew Riha, pv magazine USA), about 20 W for the BLUETTI Apex 300 (The Solar Lab; 19.5 W per Tristan Rayner, ESS News) and about 58 W for the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus (The Solar Lab), which is 0.24, 0.48 and 1.39 kWh a day taken from the battery before any appliance runs.
standout_why: I opened five of the results: the three cited pages (StormWatts 240 V solar-input comparison, Solar Waypoint F3800 vs DELTA Pro 3 vs 5000 Plus, EnergySage best solar generators) plus the StormWatts same-panel-watts kit page and Lights On Labs. The three cited pages and Lights On Labs each say they did not test, and hold only maker specs and their own arithmetic. The StormWatts kit page has one owner measurement, on a different product (Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus with 800 W of SolarSaga 200W panels peaking at 696 W). None gives a measured idle draw, measured delivered Wh or measured panel output for the Apex 300, Explorer 5000 Plus, S5000 or DELTA Pro 3. The solargenadvisor.com kit page failed to load (certificate error) and the other results were not opened, so the claim covers the five pages read.
decides: It confirms rather than decides the pick. Using ChatGPT's own assumption (4 peak sun hours, 80% charging efficiency), 1,000 W of panels harvest 3.2 kWh a day. The Jackery 5000 Plus at 58 W idle uses 1.39 kWh of that (about 43%) with the inverter left on, and the Apex 300 at 20 W uses 0.48 kWh (15%). So the BLUETTI Apex 300 + 2× B300K + 2× 500 W kit keeps more of each day's sun than the Jackery 10 kWh Home Kit with the same panel watts. The Apex 300 + 2× B300K + 2× 200 W kit loses that edge: its 400 W of panels harvest 1.28 kWh a day, and idle takes 0.48 kWh (37.5%). The S5000's 10 W idle and 680 W measured from its two bundled-type PS400 panels favour the Anker for standby-heavy home backup, but only the 5 kWh S5000 kit is in our table and it is outside the size line. All idle figures are for a single base unit; nobody measured the stacks with expansion batteries. Measured delivered energy also trims the headline size: at Outdoor Life's 83% the 8,294.4 Wh BLUETTI kit would deliver about 6.9 kWh at the AC outlets.

findings.note: Published 2026-10-28 (ESS News original 2026-10-25). Pre-release unit, Northern California. Arithmetic: 5% of 5,024 Wh = 251 Wh a day, about 10 W. Plugged in and full it drew about 7 W from the wall. No expansion battery was tested ('I didn't test them').

findings.note: Published 2026-10-28. The output side is the Anker app's reading, not a meter, so it is not directly comparable with the Kill A Watt and test-jig figures for the other stations. Wall energy was metered at the 1,800 W charge setting.

findings.label: Measured solar output of two 400 W PS400 panels in series (Andrew Riha, pv magazine USA)
